name: Apex Carbon 16
description: The all-court paddle we build the rest of the line around. A raw T700 carbon face gives you the grit for a heavy topspin roll, while the 16mm thermoformed core keeps the drop soft enough to reset under pressure.
highlights: Peel-ply raw carbon face holds grit for a full season
Foam-injected perimeter walls widen the sweet spot
Hand-balanced to a swing weight window of ±3

name: Kitchen Control 14
description: Built for the dink war. The 14mm core dampens pace on contact so blocks die in the kitchen instead of popping up, and the elongated shape adds reach on the stretch volley.
highlights: 14mm core absorbs pace for softer resets
Elongated face adds 0.6in of reach
Most-recommended paddle by our coaching partners

name: Drive Pro X
description: A head-heavy balance and a stiff face make this the paddle for players who end points from the baseline. Expect a noticeably higher launch angle on the drive.
highlights: Head-heavy balance for a heavier ball
Textured grit face rated near the spin limit
Unibody handle kills twist on off-centre hits

name: Flux Elite Edgeless
description: No edge guard, no dead zone. The moulded frame pushes the playable surface all the way to the perimeter, which is why our sponsored players keep one in the bag.
highlights: Edgeless construction, no dead perimeter
Widest measured sweet spot in the line
Ships with a matched cover

name: Rally Starter
description: The paddle we hand to anyone in their first season. Light, cheap to replace and forgiving enough that mishits still clear the net.
highlights: Lightest paddle in the line at 7.4 oz
Cushioned grip for players new to the sport
Same 30-day play test as the pro models

name: Night Shift 16
description: The Apex platform in a blacked-out limited run of 500. Same 16mm thermoformed build, matte edge guard, numbered butt cap.
shortDescription: Matte black raw carbon · limited run
highlights: Numbered run of 500
Matte edge guard and blacked-out hardware
Identical layup to the Apex Carbon 16

name: TrueFlight Outdoor 40
description: Rotationally moulded in one piece so there is no seam to split. 40 holes, tournament weight, and a flight path that stays true in wind.
highlights: Seamless one-piece mould
40 holes, outdoor tournament spec
Stays round through a full league season

name: TrueFlight Indoor 26
description: A softer compound and larger holes for gym floors. Quieter off the face and easier to control on a slick surface.
highlights: 26-hole indoor pattern
Softer compound for gym floors
Noticeably quieter off the paddle

name: Baseline Dry Tee
description: A recycled poly mesh that moves sweat off your back between points. Cut long enough to stay tucked through a full third-shot sequence.
highlights: UPF 40 sun protection
Made from 82% recycled polyester
Flatlock seams that do not chafe under a strap

name: Kitchen 7in Shorts
description: Seven-inch inseam, four-way stretch and a deep pocket on each hip sized for an outdoor ball so you are not chasing spares between games.
highlights: Two ball pockets sized for a 74mm ball
7in inseam, four-way stretch woven
Zip pocket for a key and a card

name: Court Cap
description: A five-panel cap with a perforated crown and a band that actually holds sweat off your eyes in August.
highlights: Perforated crown panels
Moisture-locked interior band
Adjustable rear strap

name: Midcourt Hoodie
description: Warm-up weight brushed loopback for cold morning sessions. Cut slim enough to play a game in before you shed it.
highlights: Brushed loopback cotton blend
Raglan sleeve for a clean swing path
Ribbed cuffs that hold their shape

name: Tour Duffel 40L
description: Forty litres, a fleece-lined sleeve for six paddles and a vented shoe well at the base so your bag does not smell like a locker room.
highlights: Fleece-lined sleeve holds six paddles
Vented shoe well at the base
Insulated side pocket for two bottles

name: Sideline Sling
description: For the session where you only need two paddles, a tube of balls and a water bottle. Sits flat against your back on the bike.
highlights: Holds two paddles and a ball tube
Single-strap quick-swing access
Water-resistant base panel

name: CourtGrip Low
description: A lateral cage that holds your foot through the split-step and a gum outsole that will not mark an indoor floor.
highlights: TPU lateral cage for hard direction changes
Non-marking gum outsole
Six-month outsole durability guarantee

name: Tacky Overgrip 3-pack
description: The overgrip our team re-wraps with every fortnight. Perforated, tacky when wet, and thin enough not to change your grip size.
highlights: Stays tacky through a sweaty session
Perforated for grip in humidity
0.6mm — will not change your grip size

name: Asics Solution Speed FF 3
description: The lightest Solution in the line. FF Blast Plus foam keeps the ride quick under the split-step, and the DYNAWALL midsole stops the foot rolling over the edge when you push wide for a backhand dink.
shortDescription: FF Blast Plus cushioning · all-court outsole
highlights: FF Blast Plus foam for a light, fast ride
DYNAWALL midsole resists roll on hard lateral pushes
Six-month outsole durability guarantee

name: Asics Solution Speed FF 3 Blackout
description: Same Solution Speed platform in a blacked-out mesh upper. The mint outsole is non-marking, so it is the pair we hand to players who split their week between a gym floor and an outdoor court.
shortDescription: Blacked-out upper · mint green sole unit
highlights: Non-marking outsole approved for indoor courts
Engineered mesh upper that dries overnight
Reinforced toe drag pad

name: Asics Gel-Dedicate 8
description: The pair most of our league players actually buy. GEL cushioning under the forefoot, a wide flat last for stability, and a price that survives being replaced every season.
highlights: GEL cushioning under the forefoot
Wide flat last for players who want stability first
Synthetic overlays hold the midfoot on a hard cut

name: Asics Gel-Dedicate 8 GS
description: The Gel-Dedicate scaled for junior feet. Lighter throughout, with a softer heel counter so a growing foot is not fighting the shoe through a two-hour coaching session.
highlights: Junior last, 30% lighter than the adult build
Softer heel counter for a growing foot
Same non-marking all-court outsole

name: Babolat Jet Tere 2 All Court
description: The fastest-feeling shoe we stock. The Matryx woven upper wraps the foot without break-in, and the Michelin compound holds grip on a dusty outdoor court long after a stock outsole has gone slick.
highlights: Matryx woven upper needs no break-in
Michelin rubber outsole for dusty outdoor courts
Lowest stack height in the shoe line

name: Babolat Jet Tere 2 Junior
description: A junior cut of the Jet Tere with the same wrap-around upper. Light enough that a ten-year-old keeps moving their feet in the third game.
highlights: Junior last with a padded collar
Single-density midsole tuned for lighter players
Non-marking outsole for school gym floors

name: Babolat Jet Tere 2 Navy
description: The Jet Tere in a full navy knit. Identical platform to the white pair — pick this one if you play on courts that turn a white upper grey in a fortnight.
shortDescription: Full navy knit · same Michelin outsole
highlights: Dark knit upper hides court dust
Michelin rubber outsole
Same fit as the white Jet Tere 2

name: Babolat Jet Mach 3
description: Babolat's flagship speed shoe. The Active Flexion upper tightens as you load into a lunge and releases when you push off, which is what makes it feel faster than its weight suggests.
highlights: Active Flexion upper tightens under load
Michelin outsole with a six-month guarantee
Kompressor shock absorption in the heel

name: Mizuno Wave Exceed Light 2
description: Nine and a half ounces with a Wave plate through the midfoot. If you play a fast hands game at the line and hate feeling anchored, this is the pair to try first.
shortDescription: Wave plate · the lightest pair we stock
highlights: 9.5 oz — the lightest shoe in the catalogue
Wave plate stiffens the midfoot without adding weight
Non-marking outsole for indoor play

name: HEAD Pro 40 Outdoor
description: HEAD's tournament outdoor ball in the standard three-ball sleeve. A hard shell that keeps its shape through a long third-shot rally and a flight that does not wobble in a crosswind.
highlights: 40-hole outdoor pattern
Hard shell holds its round through a season
Tournament weight, matched sleeve to sleeve

name: HEAD Pro 40 Outdoor · 4 sleeve case
description: Four sleeves of the Pro 40 in one case — the way club nights actually buy them. Works out cheaper per ball than the single sleeve and keeps a spare tube in every bag.
highlights: Four sealed three-ball sleeves
Cheaper per ball than a single sleeve
Same tournament spec as the single tube

name: SIXX Club 40 Outdoor
description: The ball we put out for Saturday open play. Softer than a tournament ball, which means it survives a beginner's mishit off the edge guard instead of cracking.
highlights: Softer shell that survives edge-guard hits
40-hole outdoor pattern
The cheapest ball we are willing to stock

name: SIXX Tour 40 Premium
description: SIXX's premium one-piece ball. No seam means no split, and the tighter weight tolerance is what tournament directors are actually paying for.
highlights: One-piece mould, no seam to split
Tight weight tolerance sleeve to sleeve
Approved for tournament play

name: SIXX 20-Ball Bulk Box
description: Twenty Tour 40s in a plain carton. This is what our coaching partners order when they are feeding drills four nights a week and losing balls over the fence.
highlights: Twenty Tour 40 balls in one carton
Roughly a third off the sleeve price per ball
Sized for a ball machine hopper

name: Engage Pursuit Pro1 Ember
description: Engage's control flagship. A six-layer face spreads the impact so the ball sits on the paddle a fraction longer, which is what makes the third-shot drop so repeatable with it.
shortDescription: Six-layer face · black on ember graphic
highlights: Six-layer face for a longer dwell time
Variable-release polymer core
Hand-weighted in pairs for doubles teams

name: Engage Pursuit Pro1 Ice
description: The Pursuit Pro1 in the ice colourway. Identical layup to the Ember — pick on looks, not on feel, because on court there is nothing between them.
shortDescription: Six-layer face · black on ice graphic
highlights: Six-layer face for a longer dwell time
Variable-release polymer core
Same layup as the Ember colourway
